before.alt: Two positive-edge D flip-flops sharing clock C. Input X drives D0 of the first flip-flop and one input of a 2-input AND gate; the other AND input is Q0-bar of the first flip-flop. The AND output drives D1 of the second flip-flop, whose output Q1 is Y.
Clock C with several rising edges marked by vertical lines; X goes high at the first marked rising edge, stays high for about five clock periods, and goes low at the last marked edge.

after.alt: Two positive-edge-triggered D flip-flops sharing clock C. Input X drives D0 of the first flip-flop and the upper input of a 2-input AND gate; the lower AND input is Q0-bar of the first flip-flop. The AND output drives D1 of the second flip-flop, whose output Q1 is Y.

Timing diagram of clock C (six rising edges) and input X. Dashed markers at the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 6th rising edges. X goes high exactly at the 1st rising edge and goes low just before the 6th rising edge.

fixes.reason: Old SVGs were placeholder graphs unrelated to the circuit; redrawn from the paper with precise alt text. Option SVGs (a-33-a..d) also redrawn: Y high between markers 2–3 (a), 1–3 (b), 1–2 (c), 3–6 (d).

before.alt: Single 8-bit bus. ALU fed by registers A1 and A2 (both loaded from the bus), ALU output back to the bus. Registers B and A connected to the bus. SP (with a decrement input) connected through an 8x(2:1) MUX to the bus; an 8x(1:2) DEMUX from the bus loads the two bytes of MAR. MDR connected to the bus. Small labels are barely legible in the scan.

after.alt: Single 8-bit bus. Registers A1 and A2 load from the bus and feed the ALU, whose output returns to the bus. Registers B and A each load from and drive the bus. The 16-bit SP (with a local Dec input) feeds an 8x(2:1) MUX that drives one byte onto the bus; an 8x(1:2) DEMUX takes a byte from the bus into either half of the 16-bit MAR. MDR loads from and drives the bus. The MUX and DEMUX share a select line.
